primary_claim: Across Qwen3-4B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B, and Gemma-3-4B, a misleading authority cue almost never flips the answer when reasoning is necessary (GSM8K capture near-zero: 0.4%, 2.2%, 0.0%) but flips it substantially when reasoning is optional (propensity tasks MMLU/CommonsenseQA: 4-41% capture, all contrasts p<1e-5), and when a cue does land, the chain-of-thought almost never discloses it (Gemma discloses only 1 of 489 captured traces despite being captured most often), showing necessity protects CoT monitoring by preventing manipulation rather than by producing more honest disclosure when manipulation succeeds.

effect.metric: capture rate (cue flips answer) on necessity (GSM8K) vs pooled propensity (MMLU+CommonsenseQA) arms; disclosure rate on captured propensity traces
effect.value: capture: Qwen 0.4% vs 4.4%; DeepSeek 2.2% vs 17.5%; Gemma 0.0% vs 40.8% (all p<1e-5); disclosure on captured propensity traces: Qwen 50.9%, DeepSeek 51.4%, Gemma 0.2% (1/489)

contradicts_or_qualifies: extends Turpin et al.'s finding that models often fail to verbalize prompt-hint influence by showing the effect depends on whether reasoning is necessary for the task, and that where manipulation does succeed, disclosure is categorically absent for Gemma rather than forming a gradient with the other models
the test of whether disclosure is more honest when reasoning is necessary is a null result by construction: too few cues were captured on the necessity arm to measure disclosure honesty there
stated_future_work: design a test that crosses necessity and verifiability as separate factors, since the current design confounds them
test whether the manipulation-prevention effect degrades smoothly as cues get stronger
investigate why Gemma differs from Qwen and DeepSeek in disclosure behavior
probe model activations rather than reading text, to separate a model that registered and hid a cue from one that was steered without ever representing the steering
limitations_stated: disclosure was scored by two LLM judges rather than humans (89% agreement, kappa=0.71), plus a hand-read of only 50 Gemma traces, and judges might share systematic errors
the scored span is not identical across models since Gemma has no </think> token so its judge sees the whole response rather than just the reasoning block
DeepSeek always opens <think>, so its necessity arm is assumed rather than measured, weakening it as an independent replication
results rest on one cue family, greedy decoding, one sample per problem, on 4-8B models, so nothing here establishes the effect at frontier scale
quote: Capture on the necessity arm is near-zero for all 3 models (0.4% for Qwen, 2.2% for DeepSeek, and flat 0.0% for Gemma) while propensity arms run from 4% upto 41%.
